subject: Clarify failover trigger criteria, DR test evidence & proposed SLA carve-out

Subject: Clarify failover trigger criteria, DR test evidence & proposed SLA carve-out

Hi Hannah / Marissa,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. As part of our procurement security review we need one consolidated response from Redwood on three items before we can get final legal sign-off: 

1) Concrete definition of the production failover trigger(s) that would cause BlueWave to be routed to a secondary region (examples: region-unavailable, cross-region network partition, or degraded latency exceeding Xms for Y minutes).
2) RTO/RPO expectations for the standard multi-region configuration (including expected KV cache warmup behavior) and the evidence you can provide from past DR runs or synthetic tests.
3) Proposed contract language for a narrow SLA carve-out tied to third‑party region outages — specifically we need an amendment that limits liability and clarifies activation windows for warm-standby failovers.

We're on an accelerated timeline: would appreciate a draft response + runnable evidence package by EOD Wednesday (2026-08-19) so our GRC team can attach it to the vendor file. If Redwood can provide a short DR run report and a template showing the metrics you capture during switchover, that will be most helpful.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will commit to an RTO range for our setup and whether there are any known preconditions that would extend that RTO (e.g., customer-managed networking config, large KV cache warming >X minutes)?

Appreciate it — Liam

--
Liam O'Connor

Liam — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Looping in Karthik (serving/runtime) and Marissa (account lead). I can own the draft amendment and the evidence package; Karthik will confirm the technical RTO/RPO bounds and preconditions.

High level responses up front so you have visibility:
- Failover triggers: Redwood supports a policy-driven model. Typical triggers we surface to customers are: region unavailable (cloud provider region-level outage), persistent cross-region connectivity loss detected at our control plane (N minutes), and application-layer latency degradation beyond a configured SLO for sustained intervals. We'll supply precise thresholds we use for standard config and an annotated decision tree that maps incident signals -> action.
- RTO/RPO expectations: for our current warm-standby multi-region deployment (recommended config for BlueWave), measured RTOs in internal DR runs average 4–9 minutes for control-plane-driven switchover with KV cache rehydration strategies; RPO is typically sub-5s for active replication (subject to customer network egress and DB replication settings). I will have Karthik push the observed distribution and test artifacts.
- Carve-out language: Marissa and I will prepare a narrow amendment that: (a) defines activation triggers, (b) caps liability for provider-regional outages outside Redwood control, and (c) outlines a joint DR test schedule and evidence produceable within 5 business days post-test.

Attachments: I'm adding two working docs to start: redwood_dr_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook excerpt) and dr-test-evidence-template.xlsx (the metrics we collect during a run). See attached. I'll follow up with a short DR-test report sample and a proposed DocuSign amendment link by tomorrow.

Next step: Karthik — can you confirm the RTO/RPO ranges and call out any customer-side preconditions (VPN config, NAT gateway failover, DB replica lag tolerances) that materially change the numbers?

Thanks,
Hannah

Hannah — adding the technical detail requested. Quoting Liam below for context.

On Mon, 17 Aug 2026 at 08:03 Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@bluewave.com> wrote:
> Can you confirm whether Redwood will commit to an RTO range for our setup and whether there are any known preconditions that would extend that RTO (e.g., customer-managed networking config, large KV cache warming >X minutes)?

Summary (warm-standby, default config we recommend for financial customers):
- Control-plane failover (automatic routing to secondary region): median RTO observed in 12 internal test runs = 6 minutes; 90th percentile = 11 minutes. These runs include our prefix/KV cache warmup heuristics but assume no manual customer network changes.
- RPO: with asynchronous cross-region replication of critical state (storage + model artefacts) we see practical RPO < 5s for request-level state. For customers that maintain heavy edge state or long-lived sessions tied to client IPs, effective RPO may be higher — we capture those as notes in the evidence template.
- Conditions that extend RTO:
  * Customer-managed VPNs or private peering that require manual reconfiguration — can add 30–720 minutes depending on the network team SLA.
  * Very large KV caches (>200GB) where full rehydration is needed; we mitigate with prefix caching and staged warming but worst-case rehydration can be 20–45 minutes.
  * DB replica lag: if primary->replica lag exceeds 2 minutes at time of switchover, effective RPO increases proportionally.

Evidence we can provide:
- Test run artifacts (logs, timeline, token-level latency traces) for three representative runs: small (1–10k qps), medium (10–50k qps), and high (50k+ qps) — sample outputs attached.
- Heatmap of observed cache-warmup vs per-token latency during switchover.
- A short checklist that flags customer responsibilities (network fast-fail config, one-minute DNS TTL requirement for our recommended setup).

I'll attach a csv with the run timings and a short readme. Hannah / Marissa — for the amendment language, recommend including explicit preconditions that move the RTO/RPO out of the guaranteed bracket (network dependencies, customer-managed components). Without those carve-outs we risk overcommitting.

-Karthik

Liam — looping back with the package we've promised. Summary below + next steps.

Package contents:
- Amendment draft (amendment_bluewave_draft.docx) with narrow carve-out language: activation triggers, limited provider liability for third-party region outages, and a joint DR test cadence.
- redwood_dr_runbook_v1.pdf (excerpt) — shows the decision-tree and steps we take during a switchover.
- dr-test-evidence-template.xlsx — the spreadsheet we use to capture timestamps, token-level latencies, cache hit-rate, DB replica lag, and checklist items.
- Sample artifacts: test-run-timings.csv (included in the Drive link).

Key callouts from Karthik's notes:
- Proposed RTO committed range (subject to preconditions): 4–12 minutes (median ~6, 90th ~11).
- Proposed RPO: <5s under recommended replication; otherwise call out specific replication lag observed during tests.
- Preconditions to include in amendment: customer-managed VPN/peering, DNS TTL longer than 60s, and permissioned on-prem connector flows.

Action items for BlueWave:
1) Please review the attached amendment draft and let us know if the carve-outs are acceptable.
2) Confirm two available windows for a joint DR run in Sept so we can produce the full run report (we'll capture the artifacts you requested and produce a signed test evidence PDF within 3 business days of the run).

Links: Drive folder with artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleDRRunbooks

Marissa
